title: Spectral burst entropy notes and runlog
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad for an exploratory set of runs where I (Ralph) decomposed arrival traces using short-time FFTs to see whether particular frequency bands correlate with p99 amplification on the serving runtime. This is informal — notes to self + commands + raw numbers.

Background / motivation:
- We see unexplained p99 spikes when ingest patterns have repeating microbursts (inter-burst spacing ~80-200ms).
- Hypothesis: certain periodicities (spectral energy at ~5–12Hz) align with kernel wakeups, GC pauses, or batching window interactions and cause cascade amplification.
- This doc records an initial attempt to: (1) generate controlled spectral inputs, (2) run them against a staging pool, (3) collect tail metrics + trace slices, (4) compare spectral power vs tail amplification factor.

Environment:
- Cluster: staging-dedicated-a100-8 (8x A100s), model: gpt-lite-3b-quant (int8), runtime: redwood-serving-v2.4.1 (local build), kvcache: enabled (prefill=on), batcher: adaptive, batch_timeout_ms=6
- Load generator: surgegen v0.9 (python script). Script available at GH link above.
- Obs: Receiver had token-level tracing enabled (sample_rate=0.05) and ephemeral logs collected to S3.

Experiment design:
- Input sequences: short prompt producing ~40 tokens. Keep server-side generation deterministic (seed fixed).
- Arrival patterns: synthesized using sinusoidal-modulated Poisson process. Parameters varied: base_qps = [60, 150, 300], modulation_freq_hz = [2, 6, 10, 16], modulation_depth = [0.2, 0.6, 0.9]. Each run lasted 6 minutes (3m warmup, 3m measurement).
- Each run collected: p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies (end-to-end), success rate, mean tokens/sec processed, kvcache hit ratio, GPU util, packing/batch sizes distribution, queue length histogram.

Key commands (rough):
- Start load: python surgegen.py --profile sinusoid --base_qps 150 --freq 6 --depth 0.6 --dur 360 --out traces/run-2025-02-14-150hz6d6.json
- Collect metrics: ./collect_obs.sh --run run-2025-02-14-150hz6d6 --s3 s3://staging-bursts/
- Spectral analysis: python spectral_burst.py --input traces/run-2025-02-14-150hz6d6.json --win 1.0 --step 0.1 --out analysis/150hz6d6.spec

Representative run: base_qps=150, freq=6Hz, depth=0.6 (label: 150-6Hz-0.6)
- Observed throughput (tokens/sec): 12200 ± 3%
- p50 latency: 42 ms
- p90 latency: 88 ms
- p95 latency: 130 ms
- p99 latency: 420 ms  (large tail)
- success: 99.98% (2 transient 429s during minute 2)
- kvcache hit ratio (serving side): 71% (prefill + ongoing)
- average batch size: 6.7 tokens (by request aggregation)
- queue length mean: 3.4, max observed (sampled) 23

Spectral observation (same run):
- Short-time FFT (1.0s windows, 0.1s step). Peak spectral power concentrated at 6Hz (as expected; generator). Secondary energy around harmonics 12Hz.
- I computed a "tail amplification factor" = p99 / p50 = 420/42 = 10.0.
- Across windows, tail amplification spikes aligned when spectral band power in 5–8Hz bin exceeded baseline by >3x.
- Plot: (ASCII approximate)
  time ->  |---spectral-power(6Hz)---|   |--(spike)--|
  p99     ->  [ 50ms ] [ 200ms ] [ 420ms ]
  observation: windows with higher 6Hz power often had median queue length jump and a shift toward larger batch sizes (coalescing events).

Contrast run: base_qps=150, freq=16Hz, depth=0.6 (150-16Hz-0.6)
- p50: 40 ms
- p95: 110 ms
- p99: 145 ms (much better than 6Hz case)
- kvcache hit ratio: 69%
- queue length max: 9
- Interpretation: higher frequency energy (16Hz) didn't align with big p99 amplification. Hypothesis: kernel scheduling threshold / batching window interacts with ~100ms+ periodicities but not sub-60ms ones.

Low-base run: base_qps=60, freq=6Hz, depth=0.9 (60-6Hz-0.9)
- p50: 34 ms
- p99: 180 ms (amp factor ~5.3)
- GPU util: 28% (far from saturated)
- Notes: even at low average QPS, deep modulation produces local transient bursts that amplify tail; suggests not pure utilization problem.

Other signals inspected:
- Kernel wakeups: traced via eBPF (sampled at 1ms). Windows with strong 6Hz energy showed periodic kernel scheduling bursts on the proxy process (user->sys cycles).
- GC pauses: Go runtime GC logs showed small concurrent GC spikes but not large enough to explain 400ms; GC contribution ~12–18ms in worst windows.
- Batcher behavior: When burst arrives, the batcher often increases batch size from ~3->14 for a short duration; oversized batches increase GPU kernel runtimes and queue delay cascades.

Quick heuristic extracted (for PS testing):
- If short-time spectral power in 5–8Hz band exceeds threshold T1, drop batch_timeout_ms by 50% for 15s and enable more aggressive preemption. Implement as experiment toggle in runtime.
- Threshold T1 rough: normalized power > 2.5x running median for that band (empirically from these runs).

Raw table summary (selected runs):
- 300-6Hz-0.6: p50 48ms, p95 160ms, p99 900ms, kvcache 63%, queue_max 41 (severe)
- 150-6Hz-0.6: p50 42ms, p95 130ms, p99 420ms, kvcache 71%, queue_max 23
- 150-16Hz-0.6: p50 40ms, p95 110ms, p99 145ms, kvcache 69%, queue_max 9
- 60-6Hz-0.9: p50 34ms, p95 95ms, p99 180ms, kvcache 78%, queue_max 12

Conclusions (preliminary):
- Not all bursts are equal: spectral composition matters. Periodicities in the ~5–8Hz range consistently produce worse tails than higher-frequency microbursts.
- Mechanism is likely a coupling between batching window (6ms timeout + coalescing), kernel wakeups that align with burst period, and transient queue length feedback loops that increase batch sizes and kernel runtimes.
- kvcache helps but doesn't eliminate the amplification; hit-rate differences small between runs where tails differ a lot. So caching isn't the main lever here.

Actionable next steps (short):
1) Run same spectral sweep on H100 staging nodes to see hardware sensitivity (A100 vs H100 kernel characteristics). Label runs: h100-150-6hz etc.
2) Instrument batcher to emit per-batch timestamps + preemption signals, add short trace to correlate a single oversized batch -> downstream p99.
3) Implement a runtime experiment: dynamic batch_timeout adaptively halved when spectral detector trips (A/B roll).
4) Try adding small inter-burst jitter to generator (randomize phase by ±10ms) to see if de-correlating arrivals reduces amplification (test for mitigation without runtime changes).
5) Add a small synthetic victim workload (background cheap embedding calls) to see cross-tenant coupling.

Notes to self / To log later:
- Save analysis plots: analysis/150-6Hz-0.6-power-vs-p99.png and spectrograms.
- Add a dashboard with 5–8Hz spectral gauge for future canaries.
- Talk to infra about investigating epoll/wakeup latencies on node (kernel patch level) — cc: Ivy.

Misc raw observations:
- Two transient 429s corresponded to an autoscaler decision to temporarily refuse burst traffic due to observed ephemeral overload; need to check controller traces.
- One odd run had high p99 but no spectral peak; trace shows a single long-running kernel invocation (maybe a model-side spike) — this suggests some runs are orthogonal outliers.

End of scratchpad.
Ralph
(quick, messy — will refine if we decide to pursue a full experiment set)
